headline: Congress cancels a 2024 federal land plan that had closed about 1.7 million acres in eastern Montana to new coal leasing.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Bureau of Land Management plan change for the Miles City Field Office in eastern Montana. That plan change, approved on November 20, 2024, made no acres available for coal leasing. It also took 1,745,040 acres out of consideration for coal leasing, with the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. By canceling the plan change, the law opens that land to being considered for coal leasing again.

who_it_affects.how: They can again seek federal coal leases on Bureau of Land Management land in the Miles City area of eastern Montana.
The agency can no longer enforce the 2024 plan change and cannot issue a substantially similar rule unless Congress later authorizes it.

who_it_affects.group: People living near the Miles City Field Office lands in eastern Montana
who_it_affects.how: Federal land in their area that had been closed to new coal leasing may now be considered for it.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2025; the 2024 plan change is treated as having no force or effect.
